newsitem.title: UK: European debt preferred vs US, Japan - investor poll.
newsitem.headline: European debt preferred vs US, Japan - investor poll.

text.p: European bonds proved most popular in the fourth quarter, with investors overweight in their allocations of German, British, Danish and Spanish bonds, according to a survey by Paribas Capital Markets on Monday.
Bond buyers were neutral but cautious about the U.S. market and remained negative towards Japanese debt, where the low level of nominal yields has discouraged investment, the poll showed.
The survey, undertaken between January 6 and 13, canvassed 115 multi-currency investors. The allocations were measured in an index from zero to 100, 100 being the maximum overweight.

"There has been some re-allocation of investor positions within core Europe but the result had not substantially changed the key position of being overweight of the German market and underweight the French and Belgian bond markets," said Graham McDevitt, senior bond strategist at Paribas Capital Markets.
The allocation of German and Danish bonds both gave a reading of 58, down four and nine points respectively from the previous survey in October.
Investors increased their allocation of French franc bonds by five points and Belgian franc bonds by nine points. Both showed a reading of 28 points on the index.
Ecu bonds had also increased their allocation by seven points from previously to give a neutral reading of 48.
"Exposure to the Ecu market has increased, reflecting the near total belief that EMU (European Economic and Monetary Union) will take place," McDevitt said.

Among other European bonds, sterling bonds were the most popular, with an index reading of 63, an increase of four points. McDevitt, based in London, said strong currency gains had proved a key factor.
Italian bonds too increased their allocation by three points to 53, but were down seven points on duration to 44, indicating that flows had been to the short end of the yield curve.
Elsewhere, investors' allocation of U.S. Treasuries was neutral at 52, having fallen two points from the prior survey, while duration was unchanged at 45.

"Relative to Europe, the U.S. dollar yield curve remains flat, with little change over the past year," McDevitt said. "A cautious duration view can be expected as outright bulls are forced to extend along the curve to their maximum position."

Japanese government bonds (JGBs) remained unpopular with investors giving a reading of 20, up two points from previously. Duration on JGBs continued to be short, at 36, despite the shape of the yield curve and the low level of absolute yields, McDevitt said.
